```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

# Live S3 examples are skipped during ordinary package builds.
# Set RUN_S3_VIGNETTE=true to execute them.
run_s3 <- identical(
  tolower(Sys.getenv("RUN_S3_VIGNETTE")),
  "true"
)
```

# Overview

This vignette demonstrates how to use `paws` from RStudio Workbench to:

1. Authenticate using the Workbench AWS role.
2. List readable Parquet files in Amazon S3.
3. Read a Parquet file into R.
4. Write a CSV file to the user's S3 workspace.
5. Read the uploaded file back into R.
6. Delete the test file from S3.

The examples rely on the following environment variables:

- `AWS_REGION`: AWS region, such as `us-east-1`.
- `S3_READ`: readable S3 bucket name.
- `S3_WRITE`: writable S3 bucket and user prefix.
- `RUN_S3_VIGNETTE`: set to `true` to execute the live S3 examples.

For example:

```text
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
S3_READ=ghsd-test-rstudio-workspace
S3_WRITE=ghsd-test-rstudio-workspace/home/username@example.gov
RUN_S3_VIGNETTE=true
```

Credentials are obtained automatically from the AWS role assigned to the
Workbench server. Access keys should not be hardcoded in the vignette.

```{r execution-status, echo=FALSE}
if (!run_s3) {
  cat(
    "**Note:** Live S3 examples were not executed. ",
    "Set `RUN_S3_VIGNETTE=true` to run them."
  )
}
```

# Configure the AWS clients

Read the environment configuration, create the S3 client, and verify the AWS
identity being used by the R session.

```{r configuration, eval=run_s3}
region <- Sys.getenv("AWS_REGION")

if (!nzchar(region)) {
  region <- "us-east-1"
}

read_bucket <- Sys.getenv("S3_READ")
write_path <- Sys.getenv("S3_WRITE")

if (!nzchar(read_bucket)) {
  stop("S3_READ is not set.")
}

if (!nzchar(write_path)) {
  stop("S3_WRITE is not set.")
}

s3 <- paws::s3(
  config = list(region = region)
)

identity <- paws::sts(
  config = list(region = region)
)$get_caller_identity()

identity[c("Account", "Arn")]
```

# Helper functions

## Parse an S3 bucket and prefix

`S3_WRITE` contains both the bucket and the writable user prefix. This helper
separates them for use with AWS SDK operations.

```{r helper-parse-path}
parse_s3_path <- function(path) {
  path <- sub("^s3://", "", path)

  parts <- strsplit(
    path,
    "/",
    fixed = TRUE
  )[[1]]

  list(
    bucket = parts[[1]],
    prefix = sub(
      "/+$",
      "",
      paste(parts[-1], collapse = "/")
    )
  )
}
```

## Construct an S3 object key

```{r helper-make-key}
make_s3_key <- function(prefix, file_name) {
  if (nzchar(prefix)) {
    paste(prefix, file_name, sep = "/")
  } else {
    file_name
  }
}
```

## List S3 files

A single `list_objects_v2()` request returns a maximum of 1,000 objects. This
function follows continuation tokens until all matching objects have been
collected.

```{r helper-list-files}
list_s3_files <- function(
    s3,
    bucket,
    prefix = "",
    pattern = "\\.parquet$") {

  token <- NULL
  keys <- character()

  repeat {
    request <- list(
      Bucket = bucket,
      Prefix = prefix,
      MaxKeys = 1000L
    )

    if (!is.null(token)) {
      request$ContinuationToken <- token
    }

    response <- do.call(
      s3$list_objects_v2,
      request
    )

    if (length(response$Contents)) {
      page_keys <- vapply(
        response$Contents,
        function(x) x$Key,
        character(1)
      )

      keys <- c(keys, page_keys)
    }

    if (!isTRUE(response$IsTruncated)) {
      break
    }

    token <- response$NextContinuationToken
  }

  choices <- data.frame(
    file_names = basename(keys),
    path_names = keys,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  choices <- choices[
    grepl(
      pattern,
      choices$file_names,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    ),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  rownames(choices) <- NULL

  choices
}
```

## Read a Parquet object

The object is downloaded to a temporary file and read with
`arrow::read_parquet()`.

```{r helper-read-parquet}
read_s3_parquet <- function(s3, bucket, key) {
  object <- s3$get_object(
    Bucket = bucket,
    Key = key
  )

  temporary_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")

  on.exit(
    unlink(temporary_file),
    add = TRUE
  )

  writeBin(
    object$Body,
    temporary_file
  )

  arrow::read_parquet(temporary_file)
}
```

# List available Parquet files

Set `list_prefix` to an empty string to search the entire readable bucket. A
narrower prefix can be used to improve performance.

```{r list-files, eval=run_s3}
list_prefix <- "MER_Structured_Datasets/"

choices <- list_s3_files(
  s3 = s3,
  bucket = read_bucket,
  prefix = list_prefix,
  pattern = "\\.parquet$"
)

cat("Parquet files found:", nrow(choices), "\n")

if (interactive()) {
  utils::View(choices)
}

knitr::kable(
  head(choices, 20),
  caption = "First 20 available Parquet files"
)
```

The complete set of available files remains in the `choices` data frame.

```{r choices-structure, eval=run_s3}
str(choices)
```

# Select and read a Parquet file

Select the first Parquet object whose path contains `"Ukraine"`.

```{r select-parquet, eval=run_s3}
target_file <- "Ukraine"

my_parquet <- choices$path_names[
  grepl(
    target_file,
    choices$path_names,
    fixed = TRUE
  )
][1]

stopifnot(!is.na(my_parquet))

my_parquet
```

Download and read the selected file.

```{r read-parquet, eval=run_s3}
parquet_time <- system.time({
  parquet_data <- read_s3_parquet(
    s3 = s3,
    bucket = read_bucket,
    key = my_parquet
  )
})

head(parquet_data, 5)
parquet_time
```

Retain five rows for the workspace write test.

```{r create-test-data, eval=run_s3}
my_df <- head(parquet_data, 5)
```

# Write to the user workspace

Parse the `S3_WRITE` value into its bucket and user prefix.

```{r prepare-write-location, eval=run_s3}
write_location <- parse_s3_path(write_path)

write_location
```

Create a unique object key.

```{r create-output-key, eval=run_s3}
output_key <- make_s3_key(
  write_location$prefix,
  paste0(
    "testfile_fausto_",
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"),
    ".csv"
  )
)

output_key
```

Write the test data to a temporary CSV and upload it to S3.

```{r upload-file, eval=run_s3}
output_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")

write.csv(
  my_df,
  file = output_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

upload_result <- s3$put_object(
  Bucket = write_location$bucket,
  Key = output_key,
  Body = output_file,
  ContentType = "text/csv"
)

cat(
  "Uploaded:",
  paste0(
    "s3://",
    write_location$bucket,
    "/",
    output_key
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

# Verify and read the uploaded file

Confirm that the uploaded object exists.

```{r verify-upload, eval=run_s3}
uploaded_metadata <- s3$head_object(
  Bucket = write_location$bucket,
  Key = output_key
)

uploaded_metadata[
  c(
    "ContentLength",
    "ContentType",
    "LastModified",
    "ServerSideEncryption"
  )
]
```

Download the uploaded CSV and read it back into R.

```{r read-uploaded-file, eval=run_s3}
download_result <- s3$get_object(
  Bucket = write_location$bucket,
  Key = output_key
)

download_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")

writeBin(
  download_result$Body,
  download_file
)

uploaded_data <- read.csv(
  download_file,
  check.names = FALSE
)

head(uploaded_data)
```

# Delete the test object

Delete the uploaded file after the read/write test is complete.

```{r delete-file, eval=run_s3}
delete_result <- s3$delete_object(
  Bucket = write_location$bucket,
  Key = output_key
)

cat(
  "Deleted:",
  paste0(
    "s3://",
    write_location$bucket,
    "/",
    output_key
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

Remove the local temporary files.

```{r cleanup, eval=run_s3}
unlink(
  c(
    output_file,
    download_file
  )
)
```

# Running the vignette

To execute the live S3 operations before rendering the vignette:

```r
Sys.setenv(RUN_S3_VIGNETTE = "true")

rmarkdown::render(
  "vignettes/rstudio-workbench-mve-s3.Rmd"
)
```

During an ordinary package build, leave `RUN_S3_VIGNETTE` unset. The vignette
will render the example code without executing live AWS operations.

The package `DESCRIPTION` file should include:

```text
Suggests:
    arrow,
    knitr,
    paws,
    rmarkdown

VignetteBuilder: knitr
```
